newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE's Al-Khazna insurance share allotment begins.
newsitem.headline: UAE's Al-Khazna insurance share allotment begins.

text.p: Share allotment in the United Arab Emirates' Al-Khazna Insurance Co (AKIC) would begin on Saturday after the initial flotation was oversubscribed more than 13 times, a UAE newspaper said.
About 50,000 UAE nationals applied for shares worth 2.7 billion dirhams ($750 million), the company's founding committee announced, according to the daily Gulf News on Saturday.
The nominal value of each share was 100 dirhams.

The committee said the huge demand for shares in Al-Khazna -- which would be the UAE's largest insurance firm with 380 million dirhams in authorised capital -- surpassed all expectations, the paper said.

"By the end of the 10-day flotation on August 31, a total of 49,669 nationals had subscribed to more than 26 million shares at a value of 2,720,640,000 dirhams, although only 2.09 million shares were offered," a founding committee spokesman was quoted as saying.
He declined to disclose the share allotment rate, but said the committee would begin distributing the shares based on a previously agreed percentage.
The spokesman said the new company, in which the founders would control a 45 percent stake and the public 55 percent, would hold its founding general assembly on November 10.

AKIC's public offering is the third flotation on the UAE's unofficial stock exchange since March 1995. Public offerings by Dubai Investment Co and Abu Dhabi Shipbuilding Co were three times oversubscribed. -- Dubai newsroom +9714-6071-222
